## Shots can't be outrun or dodged (2026-11-06)
Asked for: bullets should be a lot faster, and impossible to outrun or evade.

What was done:
- LaserBolt (yours, the pirates', the guards'): 2600 px/s (was 820-1000) and homing - it
  steers to its target's current position every frame, so it can't be outrun or
  sidestepped. The hit is checked before moving (at this speed it would otherwise skip
  past the target); if the target falls first, the bolt flies on and fades.
- ArcherArrow (the archer's laser arrows): 2200 px/s (was 1150) and homing too.
- Docs (pilot's guide: you can't dodge them). Test: test_shots_cannot_be_dodged - a bolt
  and an arrow fired at a target 900 px away zig-zagging at 600 px/s both hit, in under
  half a second.

Files changed: scripts/surface_props.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md

## Pirate sprites: nothing cropped (2026-11-06)
Reported: the pirate's gun is cropped out in some frames.

Cause: the cutter boxed each figure by counting figure pixels per column of the sheet
(> 25 per column) - a thin rifle barrel sticking out sideways has only a few per
column, so it fell outside the box and was cut off. Worst in frame 4 (aiming):
in some views 30-40% of the width (the whole barrel); also several views of frames 1-3.

What was done:
- Re-cut all 32 pirate pictures from the sheets with whole cells: each figure's box
  reaches 30 px short of its neighbours' middles (the outer ones 300 px out), then only
  the figure and pieces inside its outline are kept - not neighbours' parts, the angle
  labels or the sheet's legend. A check reports any figure touching its cell's edge:
  none of the views used does (frame 4's 90° does, but West is the mirrored 270°).
  E.g. aim e: 137 -> 193 px wide, aim nw 137 -> 193, aim se 151 -> 174, idle se 141 -> 149.
- The cutter kept as tools/cut_sheet_views.py (for the next sheets).
- Checked the guard and the player too: the player's are complete; the guard's crop boxes
  never touch a figure (cut by fixed boxes on the backdrop), so nothing was lost there.

Files changed: art/pirate/pirate_{idle,raise1,raise2,aim}_*.png (32, re-cut)
New files: tools/cut_sheet_views.py

## 2026-11-06 - Blender MCP connection (tooling, not in the game)
- Asked: connect Claude (VS Code extension) to Blender, to make 3D models and render sprites from them.

  socket answers (Blender 5.2.2). Godot skips hidden files, so .mcp.json is neither imported nor exported.

## 2026-11-06 - Pirate android as a 3D model in Blender (look-dev test, not yet in the game)
- Asked: delete the test sphere; model the pirate NPC in Blender, close to its sprite, with similar
  textures and materials (first step towards rendering sprites from 3D models instead of cutting sheets).
- Done: `external/blender/pirate/build_pirate.py` builds the whole pirate from scratch in Blender
  (MCP or `blender -b --python`), in the collection "Pirate" under the empty "PirateRoot":
  - 112 objects, every body part a rigid object (<part>.L / .R) so it can be parented to one bone each
    later - no weight painting needed for an android.
  - Pieces: armoured legs / boots, pelvis, belt with 3 skulls, chest with pecs and the green gem,
    backpack with glowing cells, skull-faced head with red eyes and grille, tricorn (three sides
    turned up, gold trim, spikes, skull and crossbones), spiked pauldrons, arms with vambraces, the
    rifle in the right hand (barrel down, green and yellow cells), a long coat open in front with a
    torn hem, rags on the shoulders, a high collar, 5 tentacles from the back.
  - 11 procedural materials (PIR_*): rusty bronze (pitted), dark metal, crimson cloth, leather, gold,
    bone, tentacle, glowing green / yellow / teal, red eyes.
  - Stage: 3 area lights (warm key, red rim, violet fill), dark violet world, ortho camera 30 deg above
    (the game's view), Eevee, AgX Punchy, transparent film; the default scene "Light" hidden from render.
- Renders: external/blender/pirate/preview_{front,q45,side,back}.png (900x900); the scene saved as
  external/blender/pirate/pirate.blend.
- Not in the game yet: next steps would be a rig (one bone per part), the idle / raise / fire
  animations, and rendering the 8 views per frame into art/pirate/.
- Files: external/blender/pirate/build_pirate.py, pirate.blend, preview_*.png (all new, outside the build)

## 2026-11-06 - The pirate walks (an 8-frame walk cycle from Blender)
- Asked: make a walking animation for the pirate.
- Blender (external/blender/pirate/pirate_sprites.py; scene external/blender/pirate.blend):
  - apply_walk(k): an in-place cycle of 8 frames, the rifle hanging in the left hand: thighs swing
    +-0.32 rad (18 deg), the knee bends up to 0.55 rad just after the foot passes under the body, the
    foot kept level (and toes down as it leaves the ground), the hips dip 12 mm on each contact, the
    free right arm swings against the legs, the rifle sways. One cycle = two steps = the game's
    STRIDE (64 px, ~0.52 m at the pirate's on-screen size). Axes found by probing the rig (thigh /
    knee / foot turn on local Z; hips up = local Y). First try had the knee too high behind; tuned.
  - keyframe_walk(): actions PirateWalk / PirateWalkGun / PirateWalkHand (frames 1-8, constant,
    fake user); PirateAttack stays assigned.
  - render_all now renders FRAMES = 4 attack poses + walk1..walk8, x 8 views = 96 renders (39 s),
    and writes renders/meta.json: where the character stands (its root on the ground) in the render.
- tools/sprites_from_renders.py: also writes art/<id>/<id>_anchors.json - each sprite's anchor (that
  ground point, in sprite pixels).
- scripts/sheet_puppet.gd: counts walk frames (<id>_walk1_..); with the weapon down and walking it
  plays them by phase (one cycle per stride, TAU of phase) - no faked bob / sway then; loads
  <id>_anchors.json and stands every picture on its anchor (steady through the cycle - the middle of
  the feet would jump as they move). The guard / player (no walk frames, no anchors) unchanged.
- art/pirate/: 96 sprites now (idle, raise1, raise2, aim, walk1..8 x 8 views) + pirate_anchors.json.
- Tests: new test_surface.test_pirate_walk_cycle (8 frames, one cycle per TAU and looping, no faked
  bob, anchors used, steady anchor, aiming overrides walking); test_pirates now stands the pirate
  still before checking its idle frame. 63 passed, 0 failed.
- Docs: editor.md (Library: the pirate's walk cycle).
- Files changed: scripts/sheet_puppet.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, tools/sprites_from_renders.py,
  data/docs/editor.md, art/pirate/* (96 PNG + pirate_anchors.json, 64 new);
  external/blender/pirate/pirate_sprites.py, renders/, external/blender/pirate.blend

## 2026-11-06 - Pirates fight back, and run when badly hurt
- Asked: when I attack a pirate it must attack back; a pirate low on health tries to run away.
- Done (scripts/surface_props.gd):
  - LaserBolt and ArcherArrow carry their `shooter` (set by you - Pilot.fire_at -, guards, pirates,
    archers); on a hit the target hears who it was: attacked_by(shooter).
  - SurfacePirate.attacked_by: never at another pirate; it holds a grudge (GRUDGE 15 s, up to
    GRUDGE_RANGE 1600 px) and turns on the shooter at once - raising the rifle if they're in its reach,
    else a new "chase" state closes in (CHASE_SPEED 85 px/s) until within 0.85 x RANGE, then fires.
    Mid-burst it switches to whoever is shooting it. _target() prefers its grudge.
  - At FLEE_HP (30% of 70 hp) or less: a new "flee" state - the rifle comes down (0.3 s), it runs
    straight away from the threat (FLEE_SPEED 120 px/s, slower than your 190: you can run it down),
    steering round water / walls (_step tries +-0.6, 1.2, 1.8 rad), shouts a line ("Fall back!..."),
    and stops after FLEE_SAFE 950 px or FLEE_TIME 9 s, lying low there (home = where it stopped). While
    hurt it won't pick a fight: anyone coming in reach makes it run again.
  - Works against guards and the archer too (they're shooters as well).
- Tests: new test_surface.test_pirates_fight_back_and_flee (a real bolt from you, out of its reach: it
  knows who, chases, fires back from within reach; badly hurt: runs, rifle down, no shots, slower than
  you, stops and lies low, runs again when you come near). (While writing it: an earlier test's archer
  - not in npcs - joined the fight; the pirate correctly turned on her; the test now clears everyone.)
  64 passed, 0 failed.
- Docs: game.md (Pirates).
- Files changed: scripts/surface_props.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md
